clue.text: Staid set's unusual aversion

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of 'staid set' come in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A prim, sedate group shows an odd dislike of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges STAIDSET; the 's is just a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a strong dislike or feeling of revulsion towards something.

clue.text: Announce editor's upset Irish county

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the editor's letters are turned over

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
Clare is a county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: Reporting that a newspaper editor has distressed a part of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to state or proclaim publicly.

clue.text: It's tied over in Chelsea ground

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
ground as the past of grind, so the letters of 'Chelsea' are milled into a new order

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A football match finishing level, with extra time at Chelsea's stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like Stamford Bridge, Chelsea's football stadium in London, but it is the anagram indicator; 'over' is the cricket O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a string for a shoe is knotted to keep it on.

clue.text: Spills liquid on small dishes

parts.note: platters are large serving dishes

explanation.surface: Someone splashes a drink over little plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: scatters drops of fluid messily.

clue.text: Renown oddly ignored for long time

indicators.note: oddly ignored means the odd-placed letters of 'Renown' are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Fame that is strangely forgotten over many years.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an age or immensely long period.

clue.text: Agreement leads to peace and calmer times

indicators.note: the leads of the following words are their opening letters, which are taken

explanation.surface: A treaty ushers in a quieter period of history.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a formal accord or treaty between parties.

clue.text: Artist's equipment Dad authorised with note

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
let means allowed or authorised
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A father approves a painting kit and leaves a message.
explanation.definitionFit: The board on which a painter mixes colours is part of their kit.

clue.text: Have discussion about island tree

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the talk wraps round the island

parts.note: to confer is to have a discussion

explanation.surface: Talking about a tree growing on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a cone-bearing evergreen such as a pine or fir.

clue.text: Calm Scot, bold internally

indicators.note: internally points to the inner letters of the two words 'Scot' and 'bold'

explanation.surface: A Scotsman described as composed and, underneath, brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' takes the middle pair of each word: CO from Scot, OL from bold.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: unflustered, composed, not agitated.

clue.text: Use it to communicate secure policy

parts.note: to land something, such as a contract or fish, is to secure it
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: Instructions to adopt a guaranteed policy for messaging.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a fixed telephone connection is something used for talking to people.

clue.text: Excited, bet after ace appears

indicators.note: after places the bet's letters following those of the ace

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
a flutter is a small bet

explanation.surface: A gambler gets thrilled when an ace turns up after placing a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: in a state of nervous agitation or eager anticipation.

clue.text: Storyteller near court, upset

indicators.note: upset signals the letters of 'near court' are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A spinner of tales close to the court gets distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a skilled teller of anecdotes.

clue.text: Article used in Athens

indicators.note: used in shows the letters sit inside the word 'Athens'

explanation.surface: A grammatical article that appears in the Greek capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar term: the definite article of English.

clue.text: Recluse, not married, to get older evidence from past

indicators.note: not means the married letter is left out of the recluse

parts.note: a hermit is a recluse
to age is to get older

explanation.surface: A single hermit growing old leaves traces of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Inherited traditions and buildings that bear witness to earlier times.

clue.text: Get away from ultimately remote southern headland

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of 'remote'

parts.note: a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Fleeing from an isolated promontory in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to break free or flee from confinement.

clue.text: Glib talk about a northern dog

indicators.note: about means the talk goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a spiel is slick, glib patter

explanation.surface: Smooth chatter concerning a dog from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a breed of gundog with long ears.

clue.text: Draw an area of land when talking

indicators.note: when talking means the phrase is said out loud and heard as another word

parts.note: a tract is an area of land, so the phrase is 'a tract'

explanation.surface: Sketching a plot of ground while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like sketching, but it means pull in.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to pull in or entice, as a crowd.

clue.text: Encourages outsiders in crunch elite races

indicators.note: the outsiders of each of the next three words are their first and last letters

explanation.surface: Backing given to rank outsiders in a decisive top-level competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to shout support for or spur on.

clue.text: Fight nationalist who's rising, austere

parts.note: to spar is to fight

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the nationalist's letters read upwards

explanation.surface: An ascending nationalist fighter with a severe manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: severely simple, like the frugal ancient Greeks of Sparta.

clue.text: Favourite verse writer, not old

indicators.note: not means the letter for old is left out of the writer

parts.note: a poet writes verse

explanation.surface: A beloved poet who isn't elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a preferred one, as in teacher's darling.

clue.text: Unexpected reason to embrace It girl

indicators.note: to embrace puts one piece inside another
unexpected signals that the letters of 'reason' are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A surprising explanation for hugging a fashionable young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It girl' reads as one phrase for a socialite, but it splits: 'to embrace' puts It inside SENORA (the anagram from 'Unexpected'), leaving girl as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish title for a young unmarried woman, so loosely a girl.

clue.text: Strive to protect vehicle — silver — in cleric's house

indicators.note: to protect means surrounding the inner pieces like a guard

parts.note: to vie is to compete or strive
a car is a vehicle
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Trying to guard a car and the silver in a clergyman's home.
explanation.definitionFit: The residence provided for a parish priest of the Church of England.

clue.text: Measure of land General brings up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the carried letters read upwards
brings means the word General carries the letters within it

explanation.surface: A military commander raises the subject of acreage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army rank but is just the word holding the letters, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of area equal to a hundred square metres.

clue.text: Secure period of abstinence

definitions.meaning: firmly fixed, as in stuck tight
a time of going without food, as in Lent

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: firmly fixed, and a time of going without food.

clue.text: Place (Old Testament) small land area

parts.note: PL is the street-name abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: A spot in the Bible where a little plot of ground is mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a small piece of ground, as for building or gardening.

clue.text: When speaking, you're candid about a Pole, for example

indicators.note: when speaking means the phrase is said out loud and heard as another word

parts.note: candid means open, so the phrase is 'you're open'

explanation.surface: Telling a Polish acquaintance in conversation that they are frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link; 'a Pole' looks like a stick, but it is a person from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Poland is in the continent, so its natives belong to it.
